summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel, Cas (narrator) recovers from a gunshot wound inflicted by Rio, who shot him on purpose at Cas's instruction. Cas reflects on friendship and Rio's motives, then Arthur returns and argues with Cas about Rio, insisting the shot was lethal and that Rio should not be trusted. Arthur remains at Cas's bedside, and the two keep arguing over whether getting shot was part of the plan.
one_line: Cas recovers from a gunshot wound, and Arthur angrily argues with him about Rio, who shot him on Cas's orders.
key_facts: Cas, still drugged and recovering, tells Rio that he is a good friend.
Rio replies, "I'm not your friend, Cas," and tells him not to think otherwise.
Cas reflects that friends care about you and know you well enough to communicate without words.
Arthur returns and asks Cas how he is feeling; Cas answers "Fuzzy" and asks where Rio is.
Arthur says Rio is out and that he shot Cas.
Cas says he told Rio to shoot him and that he knew he could line up a nonlethal shot.
Arthur says that any gunshot can be lethal and that a leg hit can kill.
Arthur says Rio shot Cas in the chest, and Cas almost died if the bullet had not missed his heart.
Cas says he made the bullet bounce because he told it to.
Arthur appears close to crying after Cas's remarks about the bullet.
Cas wonders why Arthur keeps hanging around, since Pithica was the only case he was working on.
Arthur says he will not leave Cas alone with someone who shot him.
Cas notes that the medical staff have taken away more of his drugs.
Cas says getting shot was the plan, and Arthur replies that getting yourself shot is not a plan.
